The render proptest uses a fixed seed, so every run since 07:09 UTC hit the same two findings. There were three causes in all, and each one is fixed here. ### 1. Writer: braced pairs behind `{` were written twice per level (render proptest `no-termination`) `gluedPart` (`src/write-inline.ts`) writes a strong or emphasis part a second time when the part's first character is the same as the one before it, so a bare mark glued to the same mark gets braced (C2-W-069). A part that is already braced starts with `{`, so after a text ending in `{` it was rewritten as well, at every nesting level. The cost doubled with each level. The fuzz input `*{{{**` (2 KB) renders to about 100 nested `` elements whose text ends in `{`; the importer's writer then ran past the 30 s case limit. The second write is now skipped when the part already opens with `{`. That write could only return the same bytes, and the `forms` bookkeeping stays as it was. fix(ui): resolve accessibility focus and contrast issues

## Summary

Fixes four UI accessibility CSS, focus visibility, and contrast issues across the desktop UI and map renderer:

- **Timeline slider focus ring (#395):** Draw an inset `2px solid var(--focus)` focus outline (`outline-offset: -2px`) on `.track input[type='range']:focus-visible` so `.track { overflow: hidden }` no longer clips the playback slider focus indicator.
- **Toggled-off HUD chip contrast (#397):** Replace button-wide `opacity: 0.55` on `.hud-chip[aria-pressed='false']` with an opaque `var(--surface-2)` background, `var(--text-2)` value text, and `var(--text-3)` at `opacity: 1` for `.label` and `.unit` so text maintains >= 4.5:1 contrast over all surfaces and light map tiles while remaining distinct from `:disabled` (`--disabled-opacity`).
- **Link focus indicators (#407):** Include `a:focus-visible` in the shared `--focus` focus-visible selector list and add `4px` padding to `.help-nav` so focus outlines on navigation links are not clipped by its scrollport.
- **Busy status & map attribution contrast (#409):** Move the `var(--bar)` pill backdrop from `.track > .busy-status span` to `.busy-status span` so `.map-card > .busy-status` and `.pane-video > .busy-status` stay >= 4.5:1 over light tiles, and raise `#attr` background/text opacity in `packages/engine/src/renderer/dom.ts` (`rgba(12, 14, 22, 0.8)` / `rgba(255,255,255,0.88)`).

## Testing

- Added regression and WCAG contrast assertions in `apps/desktop/test/ui/globals.test.ts` and `packages/engine/test/renderer/dom.test.ts`.
- Verified `npm run lint`, `npm test`, and `npm run build` pass.

fix(backend): accept all fingerprint formats in relay family lines

<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"JuliusHenke"} -->
_Requested by **ju** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_017Ymkrt3UMWyoL61AgbK44f?thread=cmsg_017Ymkrt3UMWyoL61AgbK44fFRGiDkwoAf9V3Mr5aActXB)_

## What
Old Tor versions published family entries as `$HEX=nickname` or `$HEX~nickname`, or with lowercase hex. `computeRelayFamilies` rejected these as "not supported", so relays from older descriptors that listed each other this way ended up in no family. `DeclaredFamily.of` now accepts all of these forms and normalizes them to the uppercase fingerprint. That works on both sides, for the relay that lists an entry and for the relay that confirms it. Plain nickname entries are still ignored (see #629 and #719). Current Tor versions publish only `$HEX`, so only older months change.

## Tests
`RelayFamilyUtilTest` gets one new case for each format (lowercase hex, `=nick`, `~nick`, lowercase with `~nick`) and more invalid cases (`$HEX=`, a nickname that is too long, `$HEX-nick`, hex without `$`). All 19 tests pass locally.

## Deployment notes
Only months whose families are computed after the deploy are affected: new months, and the months from 2025-04 on that the V6 migration from #719 reprocesses. Older months keep their stored families, because `computeAllMissingFamiliesAndEvictCache` skips months that already have families. Recomputing those months would change family IDs across history, so this PR leaves them as they are.

fix: make `@gunshi/plugin-i18n` an optional peer of the plugins that work without it

### Description

`@gunshi/plugin-completion`, `@gunshi/plugin-renderer` and `@gunshi/plugin-suggestion` treat the i18n plugin as optional when they run, and only their types refer to it. Their `package.json` still required it as a peer, so npm and pnpm installed `@gunshi/plugin-i18n` for everyone who installed one of them.

- `@gunshi/plugin-i18n` is now an **optional peer** of the three plugins, as `@gunshi/plugin-global` already is for `@gunshi/plugin-i18n`
- The `.d.ts` of `@gunshi/plugin-completion` and `@gunshi/plugin-renderer` had an empty `import "@gunshi/plugin-i18n"`, which is a type error with `skipLibCheck: false` where the plugin is not installed. The build now drops it. It is the only change in the built files of all packages
- `@gunshi/plugin-renderer` lists it in `devDependencies`, as the other two do, since pnpm does not install an optional peer in the workspace
- The READMEs say to install `@gunshi/plugin-i18n` to use it
- `e2e/optional-peers.spec.ts` checks the declaration in `package.json`, and that the built files do not import it

### Linked Issues

None.

### Additional context

**Compatibility**: a project that imports `@gunshi/plugin-i18n` without listing it in its own `package.json`, and got it only through this peer, needs to add it. When it is installed, its version must still match, as the official plugins are upgraded together.

Installed from packed tarballs with npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun:

| | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Without `@gunshi/plugin-i18n` | It is not installed, and the three plugins run with the same output on the four package managers |
| Types without it, `skipLibCheck: false` | Pass |
| With it | Installed, and the text is translated |

diff --git a/e2e/optional-peers.spec.ts b/e2e/optional-peers.spec.ts
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..4cf053b17
--- /dev/null
+++ b/e2e/optional-peers.spec.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@
+/**
+ * The plugins that work without `@gunshi/plugin-i18n`, as they are built.
+ *
+ * They declare it as an optional peer dependency, so that installing them does not install it. Their JavaScript and
+ * their declarations must not import it then: an import that is left in a `.d.ts` is a type error with
+ * `skipLibCheck: false` where it is not installed. Run `pnpm build` first.
+ */
+
+import { existsSync, readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
+import path from 'node:path'
+import { describe, expect, test } from 'vite-plus/test'
+
+const PACKAGES = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..', 'packages')
+const PLUGINS = ['plugin-completion', 'plugin-renderer', 'plugin-suggestion']
+const IMPORT =
+  /^\s*(?:import|export)\b.*["']@gunshi\/plugin-i18n["']|\bimport\(\s*["']@gunshi\/plugin-i18n["']/m
+
+describe.each(PLUGINS)('%s', plugin => {
+  const dir = path.join(PACKAGES, plugin)
+
+  test('declares @gunshi/plugin-i18n as an optional peer dependency', () => {
+    const pkg = JSON.parse(readFileSync(path.join(dir, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
+
+    expect(pkg.peerDependencies).toHaveProperty(['@gunshi/plugin-i18n'])
+    expect(pkg.peerDependenciesMeta?.['@gunshi/plugin-i18n']?.optional).toBe(true)
+    expect(pkg.dependencies).not.toHaveProperty(['@gunshi/plugin-i18n'])
+  })
+
+  test('does not import @gunshi/plugin-i18n from its built files', () => {
+    const lib = path.join(dir, 'lib')
+    if (!existsSync(lib)) {
+      throw new Error(`${lib} is not found. Run \`pnpm build\` first.`)
+    }
+    const files = readdirSync(lib).filter(file => /\.(?:js|d\.ts)$/.test(file))
+
+    expect(files.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)
+    const importing = files.filter(file => IMPORT.test(readFileSync(path.join(lib, file), 'utf8')))
+    expect(importing).toEqual([])
+  })
+})

fix(backend): let the sweep alone reclaim archived homes

Fixes #4629

## Problem

Archiving reclaimed the Task's home inside the archive request (`cleanUpArchived` → `retryArchivedHomes`), while the sweep reclaims the same queued generations. On a large home (a few hundred thousand files) on a slow computer the first job is still removing the set-aside copy when the sweep's job runs. The second job finds the home gone, skips the set-aside copy because it is younger than ten minutes, and reports `absent`. That pulls the queued epoch and sets `sessionHomeReclaimedAt`, so the set-aside copy is never retried and stays on disk. The timeline with debug logging is in https://github.com/nuphos/nuphos/issues/4629#issuecomment-7078195036.

## Change

Remove the in-request reclaim and leave queued homes to the sweep alone. The sweep runs on one timer and on one replica (`claimRun`), so two reclaims of one home no longer overlap. A reclaim that times out stays queued, and the next sweep removes the set-aside copy once it is older than ten minutes, which the job already does. `retryArchivedHomes` loses its session filter, which only the removed call used.

As a side effect, `PATCH /archive` no longer waits on the reclaim job: 61 s before, 41 ms after, on the same large home.

**Tradeoff (#3939).** An archived Task's home is removed by the next sweep instead of during the archive request. A fresh backend sweeps a minute after start and then hourly, so a home can now stay up to about an hour after archiving. Triggers are still removed during the request.

The in-memory Mongo fixture now treats a numeric path segment as an array index, as Mongo does, so the sweep's `'archiveHomePendingEpochs.0'` query can be tested.

## Tests

- New `archiving leaves the home to the sweep, which keeps a timed-out one queued` in `runtime-session-home.test.ts`. It fails on main, because archiving runs a reclaim job; it passes with this change. It also covers a timed-out sweep keeping the generation queued, and the next sweep finishing it.
- Existing `removes a set-aside home a killed run of the same conversation left behind` covers the job removing a set-aside copy older than ten minutes.
- `e2e:session-homes` now restarts its backend after archiving and waits for the sweep to remove the archived Task's and its sub-Task's homes, instead of expecting them gone when the request returns. The rest of the scenario is unchanged.
- The 37 test files that use the fixture pass (340 tests), and the backend typecheck passes.

## E2E (non-production, local stack)

Same repro as the issue: a Task home with ~357k files on a second computer whose processes are limited to 10% of a CPU.

| step | result |
|---|---|
| `PATCH /archive` | 200 in **41 ms** (61 s on main); home still on disk, generation still queued |
| first sweep, computer slowed | job times out after 60 s (`agent.session_home_reclaim.failed`); set-aside copy of 357,141 entries left; row keeps `pending` with one generation, `reclaimedAt: null` (on main: `pending: []` and `reclaimedAt` set, never retried) |
| computer back to full speed, next sweep after the copy is over ten minutes old | set-aside copy removed; nothing for the Task left on disk; `pending: []`, `reclaimedAt` set |

```
11:07:57.395Z archived (status 200) in 41 ms
  on disk: ["<home>: 357146 entries"]
  row: {"pending":[{"epoch":0,...}],"reclaimedAt":null}
11:10:05.009Z agent.session_home_reclaim.failed ... "timedOut":true
  on disk: ["<home>.reclaim-1795345747821-...: 357141 entries"]
  row: {"pending":[{"epoch":0,...}],"reclaimedAt":null}
11:19:41.600Z after the next sweep to empty the queue
  on disk: []
  row: {"pending":[],"reclaimedAt":"2026-11-22T11:19:35.787Z"}
PASS
```

fix(backend): log an expired run resume at warn

Fixes #4637

## What

`agent.run.redis_resume.stream_missing_after_wait` is now logged at `warn` when the resumed run's buffer has expired, which is the expected outcome of a client resuming a finished run after `FINISHED_RUN_KEY_TTL_SEC`. The client is already told the stream is gone. The other two causes of the same event, a run that never registered its stream (`orphanConfirmed`) and the attach wait timing out, still log at `error`, since both mean a live run's stream is missing.

The change is one ternary on the log level in `run-store/stream-phases.ts`.

## Verification

- Two new tests in `stream-phases.test.ts`: a resume from a non-zero index with no buffer logs `warn`, and a resume from index 0 with no buffer logs `error`. The `warn` test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- `bun test src/lib/agent/run-store`: 28 pass. Backend `tsc` clean, eslint 0 errors.
- Against a throwaway local Redis (not production), an expired resume logged `"level":"warn","event":"agent.run.redis_resume.stream_missing_after_wait"`.

Not verified: why clients resume runs that already finished. That is out of scope here.

Encode voice clips at 32 kbps so the words are audible

Closes #248

Every Supertonic clip decoded to near silence. The model's audio is fine; at 22,050 Hz and 24 kbps lame resamples to 16 kHz on its own, and its resampler leaves speech at a peak of about 10 to 40 out of 32,767.

- Clips are encoded at 32 kbps, which keeps 22,050 Hz: a real word now peaks around 13,500 at both speeds, about 2.5 KB a clip.
- The bit rate is part of the clip fingerprint, so every copy remakes its clips; the silent ones are never asked for again and the health check sweeps them as orphans. Until a word is remade, the Standard voice plays.
- New test: the encoded frame header must say MPEG-2 at 22,050 Hz. The health check test reads the bit rate from the constant.

Checks: `npm run check`, 454 unit tests, build; clips made with the fixed code decoded and measured.

fix(charts): cap monthly x-axes at 6 ticks so month labels fit at 375px

Part of #1013 (item 1). Item 3 (carousel focus) is #1028, which carries `Fixes #1013`.

## What
With about a year of monthly data, five charts drew one label per month and ran them together at 375px (2–4px overlaps, e.g. "NovDecJan…"). `monthlyXAxisProps` gave every chart without its own `xAxisProps` a 12-tick budget.

- `chart-formatters.ts`: `monthlyXAxisProps` defaults to a 4-tick budget. d3's time scale turns that into quarterly ticks for 10 to 24 months of data and monthly ticks for shorter ranges. A budget of 6 isn't enough: for 10 to 12 months d3 still picks monthly ticks, and the Year-End trend's labels touched. A caller can still pass its own `maxTicks`. The Fuel & Stats charts from #989 keep their own budget of 6.
- `formatMonthTick` labels a January tick with its year ("2026 Apr Jul Oct"). Past 24 months d3 switches to yearly ticks, and a month-only label would read "Jan Jan Jan". This also fixes the Fuel & Stats charts, which repeated "Jan" past 36 months.
- That one default covers every chart listed in #1013 item 1: `ExpenseTrendChart`, `FuelEfficiencyTrendChart`, and every `AppAreaChart`/`AppBarChart`/`AppLineChart` caller without its own `xAxisProps` (Cross-Vehicle, Year-End, Financing, Insurance, Odometer). No call site changes.
- Bar charts (band scale) label every third month. Desktop charts get the same quarterly spacing.

Item 2 (comparison labels at 320px) is accepted as is, per the wave 9 decision: 320px isn't a `UIQuality.md` target width.

## Tests
- `chart-formatters.test.ts`: the default budget is 4 and clamps to the data length; a caller can still set 12. For 10, 11, 12 and 13 months, a d3 time scale with that budget draws at most 5 labels. The 10 and 11 month cases fail with a budget of 6. For 13, 25, 36 and 48 months, no two neighbouring labels are the same, and a January tick shows its year. The 25, 36 and 48 month cases fail with a month-only label.
- Ran the chart, analytics, financing, vehicle and dashboard component tests: 42 files, 407 tests pass.

## Measured overlap (seeded demo data, 13 months)
Worst gap between neighbouring x-axis labels, in px. A positive number is an overlap, a negative one a gap. The numbers are the same in every theme and mode.

| Chart | 375px before | 375px after |
|---|---|---|
| Cross-Vehicle, Monthly Expense Trends | 4 | −40 |
| Cross-Vehicle, Fuel Efficiency Comparison | 2 | −45 |
| Cross-Vehicle, Loan Payment Breakdown | 4 | −34 |
| Vehicle page, Expense Trends | 4 | −40 |
| Vehicle page, Fuel Efficiency | 2 | −45 |

The other monthly charts with the change, Default light and dark at 375px: dashboard Monthly Expense Trends (about 2 years, quarterly with year labels), Insurance Monthly Premium Trends (6 months, monthly), Year-End trend (11 months, now quarterly). The Odometer chart isn't shown because the seed has too few readings to draw it.
